source_candidate.title: Adelie penguin breeding population arrival chronology on Humble Island, 1991-2026
source_candidate.historical_sampling_description: Palmer LTER standard sampling describes breeding-adult arrival chronology on Humble Island approximately every two days from 1 October to 15 November.

purpose: Determine, before inspecting arrival-count values, whether HUMPOP can provide an independent colony-level process endpoint linking prior reproductive performance to subsequent breeder return/settlement timing.

allowed_before_decision: whether repeated within-season observation dates are present
prohibited_before_decision: selection of years or colonies based on observed arrival behavior

gate.GO_colony_process_test: Require a raw colony identifier that can be mapped without aggregation or manual recoding to the existing Humble colony_code frame, repeated observation dates within breeding season, and a numeric breeder abundance / occupied-nest quantity suitable for reconstructing an arrival curve.
gate.BACKGROUND_ONLY: If data contain only Humble-island totals or an island-wide arrival index with no colony identifier, use only as descriptive phenology context; do not use it to explain colony redistribution.
gate.STOP: If colony identity cannot be linked objectively, within-season effort/meaning is undocumented, or the count field is not interpretable as breeding-adult arrival/occupancy, do not analyze the outcome.

frozen_analysis_if_GO.population: Humble Island colony codes with an eligible reproductive-performance state in breeding season t and a reconstructable arrival curve in season t+1.
frozen_analysis_if_GO.predictor: S_i,t, exactly the relative reproductive-performance state frozen in PALMER_PERFORMANCE_REDISTRIBUTION_LAGS_V2.
frozen_analysis_if_GO.prior_size_control: z(log1p breeding pairs_i,t) from the independent November adult census.

arrival_curve.season_alignment: Use the dataset's documented breeding-season identifier if available; otherwise freeze a deterministic mapping from observation date to austral breeding season before reading count values.
arrival_curve.normalization: For each colony-season, divide each arrival count by the maximum observed count for that colony-season after applying only documented missing-value rules.
arrival_curve.monotonicity: Do not force the raw series to be monotone. The primary endpoint uses the first observed crossing of 0.5 of the season maximum; if the series never has at least one observation below 0.5 and one at/above 0.5, that colony-season is not estimable.
arrival_curve.primary_endpoint: arrival_midpoint_day = linearly interpolated date of the first 50% crossing, expressed as days from 1 October.
secondary_endpoints: first observation date with normalized abundance >= 0.25
first observation date with normalized abundance >= 0.75

frozen_analysis_if_GO.primary_model: arrival_midpoint_day_i,t+1 = beta * S_i,t + gamma * z_log_size_i,t + colony_code fixed effect + arrival-season fixed effect + error.
frozen_analysis_if_GO.prediction: beta < 0: colonies with better prior reproductive performance reach half of their season maximum earlier in the following spring.

primary_inference.null: Within each predictor breeding season t, colony labels of S_i,t are exchangeable with respect to next-season arrival timing after the frozen controls.
primary_inference.permutation: Permute S_i,t among eligible Humble colonies within predictor season; preserve all arrival data, missingness and controls.
primary_inference.p_value: one-sided lower-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

sensitivities: exclude colony-seasons with fewer than 4 within-season observations
repeat after requiring prior adult breeding-pair count >= 2

interpretation_if_GO.supported: Prior colony performance predicts the timing at which breeders accumulate at that colony in the following spring, providing an independent return/settlement-process correlate of the previously observed history-dependent redistribution.
interpretation_if_GO.not_supported: Do not use aggregate arrival chronology to support adult retention/settlement as the carrier of demographic history.

claim_boundaries: Earlier colony-level arrival would not distinguish returning experienced breeders from immigrants or prospectors unless individual IDs are present.
An island-total arrival curve cannot test colony-specific public information.
Arrival timing is not equivalent to survival, recruitment, or breeding dispersal.
Do not change the 50% crossing endpoint, model controls or permutation scheme after arrival-count values are opened.
The individual movement data gate remains blocked unless a longitudinal resight table with individual IDs and locations is identified.
